name: Art and Politics
description:
Since ancient times, the phenomenon of deliberate destruction of art and buildings has been observed. Even in recent times, the destruction of cultural heritage during armed conflicts, such as in the wars in the former Yugoslavia and currently in Ukraine, but also through iconoclastic, media-staged acts by terrorist groups such as IS, cannot be prevented despite improved legal protection mechanisms.
The seminar will examine the motives leading to the destruction of cultural property and analyze available instruments to protect cultural property or sanction its destruction.

The course covers the following topics:
- Motives of deliberate destruction in past and present
- The role of the black market for art
- Measures and instruments to protect cultural heritage 
- Examples of practical projects to protect cultural heritage
